subject: gov.regional
name: AFRINIC governance and receivership
status: Implemented, board contested and the receiver undischarged
milestone: Police forgery investigation confirmed 2026-08-27
position_start: Under an appeal-court order of 15 October 2024 directing the Official Receiver to complete the board election within two months, in substitution for the six months ordered in September 2023; no reconstituted board at the window's start, six months past that deadline
position_end: The regional internet registry named a person to all eight board seats on 12 September 2025 while withholding every candidate vote tally its own election guidelines promised; the purported board and the undischarged receiver announced close collaboration from 13 October 2025 without publishing which office could sign, pay or veto, and no court order, delegation, bank mandate or responsibility matrix has been located behind it; the receiver appointed an audit firm on 13 October 2025 to audit three overdue financial years without an annual meeting, with no published appointment date, executed instrument, statutory route, remuneration decision or independence review; ordinary resolutions on US$3.29m of disputed legal spending, put to the June 2026 annual meeting, were still unresolved on the public record 46 days later, and a January 2022 board resolution undertaking to bear all legal costs of a director in the Cloud Innovation litigation, carried seven votes to none, has never been closed out on the public record with a beneficiary, engagement, cap, invoice, payment or statutory classification; six regional members were named to a bylaws review committee without disclosing which constituents each represents; a member's challenge to the board's ratification of a policy draft remains open with an interim application declined and no reasoned merits decision; the appeal court set aside the registry's 2023 appeal for want of corporate authority without ruling on the receiver's permission or on statutory leave; a governance committee of three elected and two board-appointed voting members was constituted on 17 August 2026 on terms running to the ends of 2027, 2028 and 2029; the board, with the receiver's consent, named Mike Silber chief executive designate on 24 August 2026 for an assumption of office on 1 January 2027; and the Mauritius Police Force's Central CID confirmed on 27 August 2026 that two alleged forgery cases arising from the annulled June 2025 board election remain under investigation, the registry having never stated its reasons for the annulment
note: the judgment setting aside the 2023 appeal is now held in full; the account of the registry's filings is one outlet's documentary analysis alongside the registry's own announcements; the forgery investigation is confirmed by a police spokesperson to a single publication, and the two irregularities it arises from were reported by a national ISP association, not adjudicated

subject: gov.standards
name: AFRINIC Constitution (Bylaws)
milestone: Third consultation round opened 2026-08-25, closing 30 August
position_start: Fifth version in force since December 2020, with no review under way
position_end: The Bylaws Review Committee ran a first consultation from 2026-04-20, extended on 2026-05-08 to close 2026-05-17, published a draft amended Constitution on 2026-08-04 for a second consultation that closed 2026-08-21, and opened a third round on 2026-08-25 closing 30 August while it reviews the second round's submissions. It has now obtained an independent external legal opinion on a dispute resolution clause and on the legality of the board's discretionary power to terminate resource membership, and states that it does not at this stage intend to recommend a dispute resolution clause and is considering options to strengthen the safeguards on the termination power; the opinion itself is withheld as privileged. The draft's Article 24, governing law and dispute resolution, was still blank in the 53-page draft members were asked to review provision by provision, carrying only a bracketed note that advice had been sought. A new Article 3 would write into the constitution that AFRINIC is the Regional Internet Registry for Africa and the Indian Ocean and that its governance will be periodically reviewed against internationally recognised governance standards; proposed article 9.8 would let a two-thirds board vote revoke the nomination committee and restart an election the board itself had judged to have failed; the current rule barring a conflicted director from voting would be dropped and recusal relocated into board policy, which matters because Mauritius company law lets an interested director vote after disclosure unless the constitution says otherwise; article 16 opens a wide advice channel with no register of advice given or received; and article 17.5 would create an acting chief executive office with no maximum term. The published-draft milestone slipped about six weeks against the Committee's own indicative timetable while the Special General Members Meeting stayed in September 2026, and no consolidation or analysis of any round's submissions is published
note: the external legal opinion on Article 24 and on the termination power is withheld as privileged, so the Committee's conclusions on both are published without the reasoning behind them

subject: gov.standards
name: AFRINIC IPv4 policy proposal AFPUB-2026-IPv4-002 (waiver of the 90% utilisation threshold)
milestone: Moved to Last Call on rough consensus at AFRINIC-37
position_end: Draft 1 dated 6 May 2026 and Draft 2 dated 16 June 2026, presented on 24 June and moved to Last Call on rough consensus at AFRINIC-37, still a proposal rather than an implemented exception as at 23 August 2026. It would waive the Exhaustion Phase requirement to demonstrate at least 90% use of all prior IPv4 resources where a demonstrated key technical purpose - redundancy, high availability, IPv6 transition mechanisms, expansion to new sites - cannot practically be served from existing resources, treating such a request like a first allocation; the whole evidence rule is that the justification be sufficiently documented, the registry's head of member services having drawn the boundary that technical constraints may support the exception and operational ones may not, and the author having declined to publish any universal document list
note: the proposal's stages are dated by one outlet's analysis of the registry's policy docket rather than by a registry statement; the case for the waiver traces to the registry's own 2018 Policy Implementation Experience Report, where an end user was refused an additional /24 for a redundant second data centre because aggregate use was under 90%

note: funded jointly by a philanthropic foundation, two American technology companies and an African research collective; no single total is published and the individual shares are not disclosed, so the programme's size can only be bounded from the per-award ceiling

subject: finance.new
name: Mergers and acquisitions in the digital economy
milestone: 84 deals to 2026-08-17, past the 68 of all 2025
position_end: 84 deals worth an estimated US$11.4bn in disclosed value between 1 January and 17 August 2026
note: a trade-research count rather than a regulatory or exchange series, and disclosed value only, so undisclosed consideration is missing from the total; financial services led on 27 deals and the targets were concentrated in South Africa (22), Nigeria (12) and Egypt (12), with MTN Group's proposed US$6.2bn purchase of 75% of IHS Towers the largest single disclosed value. Set against US$1.44bn raised by startups in the first half of 2026 on the same publisher's count

subject: finance.new
name: Share of funded African tech startups led by a female chief executive
milestone: Third edition of the publisher's gender series, 2026-08-05
position_start: 17 of 178 funded ventures, 9.6%, taking 7.9% of the capital (2025)
position_end: 5 of 60, 8.3%, taking 2.8% of the capital (2026 to May)
note: the publisher's own count contradicts the 20.2% printed in its funding report's callout; the counts are the figures that reconcile, and the series runs 11.7% (2021), 10.9% (2022), 15.3% (2023), 12.5% (2024)

subject: finance.new
name: Stage mix of a development financier's African portfolio
milestone: Fourteen investments examined, August 2026
position_end: 79% of one development financier's African deals are at Series B or later, so it operates less like a venture fund than a later-stage investor
note: an outlet's analysis across fourteen examined investments rather than the financier's own disclosure; it measures one institution and is not a market rate

subject: finance.new
name: TaxDev III (IFS tax and social-protection policy data programme)
milestone: Running 2023-2030, US$6.36m disbursed across 29 transactions (as at 2026-08)
position_end: Institute for Fiscal Studies programme, funded by the UK's FCDO, building tax and social-protection policy data resources and tools with finance ministries and revenue authorities in Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda and Uganda; about US$6.36m disbursed 2023-2026

subject: finance.new
name: Wind-down of a blockchain backer of African startups
milestone: Chain to be discontinued 31 October 2026
position_start: An operating blockchain with a fund and accelerator pipeline backing African early-stage companies
position_end: The Swiss operator said on 25 August 2026 that it will discontinue its blockchain on 31 October 2026 and wind down its governance organisation, ending a funding and accelerator pipeline that had backed African companies in Nigeria, South Africa and Rwanda; it cited chain revenue insufficient to support its token, proposes burning 100 million tokens to cut supply from 400 million to 300 million, and has arranged a migration path for projects onto another chain. African blockchain startups raised US$90.1m in 2025, down 26.6% on the year

subject: infra.connect
name: 2026 Abuja Declaration on Meaningful Connectivity for Africa
milestone: Adopted at the CPL-26 ministerial meeting, 2026-07-24
position_end: Adopted, committing member states to technology-neutral regulation, continental harmonisation, fair access to spectrum and fibre, shared infrastructure and data governance; the text itself is not published
note: The full text was sought by the acquisition pass on 2026-07-30 and not obtained

subject: infra.connect
name: Africa Digital Connectivity Infrastructure Report
milestone: Request for proposal for Phase 1 issued 2026-08-03, closing 2026-08-18
position_end: Phase 1, Country Pilots, put out as an open consultancy tender at a stated budget of US$165,000, funded jointly by the African Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the Multilateral Cooperation Center for Development Finance; the pilot countries and the terms of reference are not established
note: The terms of reference sit behind the AIIB procurement portal and were not retrievable at ingest; an acquisition line was filed 2026-08-09

subject: infra.connect
name: Commercial 5G deployment and adoption across the continent
milestone: Industry association market study, 2026-07-22
position_end: 61 operators across 37 African markets had launched commercial 5G services by the end of May 2026, 40 of them also running 5G fixed wireless access, after first launches in Algeria, Comoros, Egypt, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia over the preceding twelve months; 5G connections in Africa are put at just under 100 million by the end of 2026, 6.2% of total mobile connections, against a projected 3.4 billion and 37% worldwide, and among sixteen focus countries only Mauritius and South Africa had 5G population coverage above 50% as of May 2026
note: an industry association's own market study and forecasts; the connection figures for end-2026 are projections, not measurements

subject: infra.connect
name: Harmonised national broadband mapping project
milestone: Intermediate training delivered at Lilongwe, August 2026
position_end: A 2025-2028 project to establish or strengthen harmonised national broadband mapping systems in eleven sub-Saharan regulators - Benin, Botswana, Burundi, Ethiopia, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe - with a five-day intermediate GIS and data-management training opened at Lilongwe for practitioners from Malawi, Zimbabwe, Botswana and Zambia, hosted by the Malawian regulator and supported by the European Union

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile internet users and their measured economic value
milestone: Industry association figures cited 2026-08-12
position_end: 416 million Africans used mobile internet in 2025, generating a measured US$240bn of economic value, put at 7.8% of continental GDP
note: an industry association’s own modelled value, cited in a secondary account

subject: infra.store
name: Continental dependence on foreign public cloud
milestone: Concentration risk set out by a cloud infrastructure specialist, August 2026
position_end: African artificial-intelligence startups are exposed to hidden financial and operational risk where a large share of workloads sits with a single provider, against which a new generation of African-founded sovereign and low-latency cloud providers is emerging
note: an expert's characterisation and an outlet's roundup; no continental measure of workload concentration, switching cost or outage exposure is held

subject: infra.store
name: Data centres the AfCFTA Secretariat states digital trade requires
position_end: More than 700, against about 220 on the continent, on the Secretary General's statement at Marrakech
sources: 2026-04-08 Africa's digital trade push requires 700 data centres, says AfCFTA chief
note: The Secretariat's own estimate, not an independent count

subject: infra.store
name: Sovereign AI cloud on edge data centres
milestone: Ranked 36th on the global supercomputer list, August 2026
position_end: The operator's AI factory is ranked 36th on the global list of the most powerful supercomputers, presented as evidence that African organisations can train and deploy models on infrastructure sited on the continent rather than abroad; the underlying offer remains AI processing units hosted inside an African edge data-centre network and sold as locally-hosted enterprise AI
note: a ranking is a capability measure and not a utilisation one; no customer count, occupancy or workload figure is published

subject: infra.store
name: Time for a data centre to reach 85% occupancy
position_end: Six to eight years in African markets against two to three in Europe, on the Africa Data Centres Association's 2026 Economic Report, which also puts 80-90% of the continent's data as still processed and stored abroad and projects the market at US$9.2bn by 2029
note: An industry association's own report; the occupancy and offshore-processing figures carry no stated method.

subject: infra.energy
name: Digitisation priorities in the national energy compacts
milestone: Constraint analysis published August 2026
position_end: The smart-metering and grid-optimisation priorities set out in the national energy compacts are argued to be constrained across Africa by a fragmented low-power internet-of-things layer: narrowband deployment reaches only markets such as South Africa, Kenya and Nigeria, while the 2G and 3G networks early smart meters rely on are expected to be retired well inside a meter's ten to fifteen year life; the analysis calls for integrated energy and telecom planning, targeted incentives for low-power wide-area network rollout, and energy-telecom co-investment
note: the count of published compacts is not settled: 29 on this source, 35 from the same author on 2026-08-11, and 30 launched on the financier's own count at 2026-06-16

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Privileged access management for the African Union Commission's own networks
milestone: Bid deadline moved from 27 August to 10 September 2026 by Addendum 01
position_end: A request for bids for the supply and installation of a privileged access management solution for the Commission's own networks (Ref. ET-AUC-560865-GO-RFB), amended on 21 August 2026 to push the bid deadline from 27 August to 10 September 2026 and to restate the licence requirement as 8 administrator, 40 enterprise privileged-user, 25 business-user and 5 external-vendor subscriptions on three-year terms, with training raised from six staff to eight
note: a procurement rather than an award; no budget, supplier or installation date is published

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Reported cybercrime losses across the continent
milestone: Continental cyberthreat assessment reported 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-13
position_end: About US$484m reported, more than double the 2024 figure, drawn from 36 member countries, with artificial intelligence involved in 55% of surveyed 2025 cybercrime cases and deepfake incidents up sevenfold between the second and fourth quarters of 2024; against that, only 8% of intelligence analysts are recorded as having advanced artificial-intelligence expertise and 94% of agencies as lacking digital forensics tools, and a single Ugandan deepfake investment scam is put at over US$2m of losses
note: the figures are an international police organisation’s own assessment, reaching the base through two secondary accounts

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Standing in the global cybersecurity index
milestone: Index released September 2024
position_end: Mauritius, Rwanda, Kenya, Tanzania and Ghana in the top tier; Benin, Togo, Zambia and South Africa in the second; the majority of the continent below, scored across legal, technical and organisational measures, capacity building and international cooperation
note: a secondary account of the index rather than the index itself, and it names only the countries it discusses

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Vendor-measured attack volume across the continent
milestone: July 2026 reading published 2026-08-13
position_end: African organisations averaged 3,237 attacks a week in July 2026 against a global average of 2,336, behind Latin America at 3,561 and Asia-Pacific at 3,316; Angola was highest of the African markets broken out at 5,714, then Nigeria at 4,975, Kenya at 2,915 and South Africa at 2,195. Ransomware victims were up 87% year on year and the continent posted the world's highest phishing rate at 1 in 106 emails
note: a single vendor's telemetry from its own installed base, not a national or continental measurement; the sample, denominator and country coverage are not published, and it is a different series from the reported-loss figures collected from member countries

subject: dpi.exchange
name: ADAPT (Africa Digital Access and Public Infrastructure for Trade)
milestone: Stated in pilot in Nigeria, Kenya and Morocco, second Digital Trade Forum, Lagos, 2026-07-02
position_end: In pilot in Nigeria, Kenya and Morocco on the Secretary-General's statement to the second Digital Trade Forum; no live exchange, governing instrument or assessment held
note: Held through Data Landscapers analysis, which is cited as named third-party analysis; the pilot is stated by the Secretary-General and no implementation document is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: AfCFTA Customs Modernisation Project
milestone: US$3.1bn contract signed with a private supplier
position_end: A public-private partnership under which Bergmans Security Consultants and Supplies Limited mobilises the financing for customs digital solutions, secure electronic exchange of customs information, coordinated border management, One Stop Border Posts, transit systems, electronic cargo tracking, non-intrusive inspection technology, integrated data centres, multilingual customs portals, risk management and data analytics across participating State Parties; the agreement builds on a memorandum of understanding concluded in July 2026 and nothing is recorded as deployed; a US$3.1bn contract was signed with a Nigerian security consultancy to digitise customs across the 50 member states, aiming at real-time cargo tracking and reduced revenue leakage
note: The concession agreement is not published; how Bergmans is repaid over twenty years, which State Parties have acceded and on what instrument, and who controls the data in the integrated data centres are stated by neither party. The Secretary-General's figure of about 50 countries signed on is uncorroborated and no list is published; the contract value and the supplier come from a press account rather than a published award notice, and the same account frames payment friction as the larger trade barrier

subject: dpi.exchange
name: AU Data Policy Framework
milestone: Endorsed by the AU Executive Council, February 2022
position_start: In force since February 2022 as the continental reference for data governance, with none of its operative texts drafted
position_end: Unchanged in text; the three operative frameworks it provides for went to validation in December 2025 and none is adopted or published
note: The English file on au.int is a 2024 reissue of the February 2022 instrument, not a later edition

subject: dpi.exchange
name: AU Digital Agriculture Strategy implementation
milestone: Continental harmonisation workshop held 11 to 13 August 2026
position_start: Adopted for 2024-2030 with an average agricultural growth target of 6 per cent and an estimated US$165 million continental implementation cost, prioritising national e-agriculture strategies over a uniform regional approach after a 2021 situation analysis covering all 55 member states
position_end: A continental workshop convened regional economic communities, union organs and participating countries to harmonise implementation, seeking interoperable agricultural data platforms, common data governance and alignment of national and regional systems with the continental digital transformation strategy and agriculture reporting
note: no member-state implementation count or timetable is published; the US$165 million is the strategy’s own continental estimate rather than a committed funding line

subject: dpi.exchange
name: AU Guidelines for Integrating Data Provisions in Protocols on Digital Trade
milestone: Issued September 2023
position_start: Issued September 2023 as a reference guide for negotiators integrating data provisions into the AfCFTA Protocol on Digital Trade
position_end: Unchanged; no record is held of its provisions being carried into the Protocol or its annexes
note: The cover date is September 2023; the AU posted the document on 2025-05-22

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Continental data governance frameworks
milestone: Validation workshop, Addis Ababa, 1-4 December 2025
position_end: Three drafts - data categorisation and data sharing, cross-border data flows, and a continental open data strategy - validated with member states and regional economic communities; none submitted to AU policy organs and none published
note: Run under the Data Governance in Africa Initiative, funded by BMZ and the European Union and implemented with AUDA-NEPAD and GIZ

subject: dpi.exchange
name: IGAD SDMX regional statistical-systems capacity-building programme
milestone: Four-day capacity-building and technical-assistance programme on SDMX convened by the Secretariat, supported by the African Development Bank
position_end: Outcome stated as harmonised SDMX Data Structure Definitions and a long-term roadmap institutionalising SDMX across IGAD and its member states under Open Data Portal 2.0; no budget, adoption date or roadmap milestone published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Member-state implementation status of the AU Data Policy Framework

subject: dpi.exchange
name: SADX (Smart Africa Data Exchange)
milestone: Cross-border digital identity pilot running between Rwanda, Ghana and Benin
position_end: Unveiled at Conakry on 2025-11-12 and taken into a technical mission with Rwanda, Benin and Ghana on trust chains, interface contracts and incident response; no live exchange held; the alliance and a German development agency say a digital identity issued in one of Rwanda, Ghana or Benin is now recognised in the other two, with eighteen further countries said to be joining, presented as the first step to a single African digital market by 2030
sources: 2026-08-11-giz-smart-africa-digital-sovereignty-interview|2026-04-27 Smart Africa drives cross-border data interoperability through SADX Technical Mission|2025-11-19 Transform Africa Summit 2025 (Conakry) - Simandou 2040 Pillar 3, TELEMO, SANIA-SADX and the closing wrap

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Smart Africa cross-border data exchange guidelines
milestone: Drafted by eleven member states at Rabat, 2025-07
position_start: Drafted by eleven member states under the Council of African IT Agencies
position_end: No adopted text, signatory list or implementation record held in the year since the drafting session
sources: 2025-07-14 Smart Africa co-creates Africa's first Cross-Border Data Exchange Guidelines (Rabat, ADD-chaired CAITA)

subject: dpi.id
name: ADLI cohort on the AfCFTA Digital Identity Annex
milestone: Cohort convened with the AfCFTA Secretariat
position_end: Six countries across three trade corridors working on compliance with the annex, on a test-and-learn basis; no assessment or mutual-recognition decision held
sources: 2026-05-27 Africa's economic future hinges on breaking down silos. This ADLI cohort advances integration

subject: dpi.id
name: Adults holding official identification in Sub-Saharan Africa
milestone: 2025 Findex round, published in the 2025 global dataset
position_end: 81% of adults, 82% of men against 79% of women, a 3.56-point gender gap (2025)
note: a survey aggregate over adults rather than a register count, and the country spread beneath it is wide - Togo and Tanzania at 62%, Uganda 67%, Zimbabwe 91%

subject: dpi.id
name: APAI-CRVS (Africa Programme on Accelerated Improvement of Civil Registration and Vital Statistics)
milestone: The 2017-2026 APAI-CRVS decade closing and a 2027-2036 phase opening, reported 2026-08-10
position_end: The 2017-2026 decade is closing and a 2027-2036 phase is opening; the African eCRVS Shared Asset (ACSA) is named as the shared continental standard intended to cut fragmented digital procurement across country systems, and Equatorial Guinea's Justice Ministry timed a free registration campaign for children aged 0-5 (10-14 August 2026) to the decade's close. No AU statement of the new phase's content, financing or targets is held
note: Both sources are secondary to the AU: a practitioner argument piece and a member-state campaign notice. The APAI-CRVS phase documents themselves are not held, so the new phase is recorded as opening rather than as adopted

subject: dpi.id
name: Continental ID and data-protection law analyser
milestone: Launched 2026-08-11
position_end: An open-source tool launched by a university research network comparing identity and data-protection laws across more than 50 African countries, built as a retrieval-augmented chatbot and stated as intended to help states harmonise their frameworks; no usage figure, governance arrangement or maintenance commitment is published

subject: dpi.id
name: Smart Africa digital identity blueprint
milestone: First edition published 2020
position_end: The alliance secretariat's first-edition blueprint for mutually recognised digital identity across member states, setting out the trust alliance, levels of assurance and the case for interoperable identity, drawn up after a member-state workshop
note: the document dates itself only to 2020 and no later edition is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: African take-up of China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System
milestone: Reported take-up across African banks 2026-08-16
position_end: Reported as spreading across African banks as an alternative to Swift, smoothing trade settlement and potentially easing exposure to dollar sanctions, with Libyan banks set to join after talks between the Central Bank of Libya and the People's Bank of China. No participant list, transaction volume or value is held
note: a single newspaper account; no operator or central-bank statement of African participation is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Association of African Central Banks (AACB)
milestone: 47th Assembly of Governors, Yaounde, 2025-11-28
position_start: No decision of the Assembly on continental payment harmonisation held
position_end: A list of 54 decisions, of which decision 21 rules that the Payment Systems Directive for Africa is not to be led by an entity external to central banks and directs its own task force to lead the work

subject: dpi.pay
name: Banks and countries connected to PAPSS
position_start: 28 banks within nine months of launch, against an ambition of all 500 to 600 African banks (2022)
position_end: 28 countries and over 190 banks and financial-technology firms connected, with the Central African central bank acceding in July 2026 and the West African central bank's pilot pending; connecting the EAC, West, Central and Southern African regional systems is put at reaching more than 60% of African countries, and no continent-wide transaction value is published (2026-08)
sources: 2026-06-01-papss-payments-network-coverage-june-2026|2026-08-17-africa-single-payments-market-currencies-divided|2026-08-10-telegraph-papss-africa-financial-system-beyond-dollar|2026-02-04 PAPSS, Onafriq launch new trade rail for West Africa|2026-03-02 Pesalink and PAPSS link networks for African payments|2022-08-30 Pan-African Payment and Settlement System drives Africa's banking integration
note: the network's own June 2026 coverage list is now held, so the reach can be read participant by participant rather than only as a count - and it records member states with no live bank or wallet at all

subject: dpi.pay
name: CARICOM Payment and Settlement System (CAPSS)
milestone: Barbados and the Bahamas central banks complete proof of concept; Ghana proposes Caribbean access to AfCFTA with local-currency settlement, Kingston, 2026-08-02
position_start: Did not exist; modelled on PAPSS since CARICOM governors' unanimous October 2023 selection
position_end: Proof of concept complete in two countries; the ECCB Governor says at least two more central banks are needed for the initial pilot; not commercially operational, with settlement, FX, liquidity, AML and interoperability arrangements unresolved

subject: dpi.pay
name: COMESA digital retail payments platform
milestone: Platform engineering vacancies advertised 2026-08-24
position_end: The regional clearing house published the scheme rulebook setting operational and governance rules for instant low-cost cross-border retail payments, and a gender audit and strategy to 2030 drawn from research along the Malawi-Zambia corridor; it advertised three platform posts on 24 August 2026 - head of technology, platform and infrastructure engineer and security engineer - whose duties establish that the platform is built on Mojaloop, runs an AWS production environment against an on-premises staging footprint and Kubernetes clusters, and that the engineering, infrastructure and information-security functions are being recruited rather than staffed
note: advisory and technical support from a private foundation and an open-source payments foundation; no transaction volume, participant count, fee schedule or go-live date is published, and the platform's technical state is inferred from recruitment advertisements rather than stated by the operator

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cost of sending money within Africa
position_end: Put at 8.78% of the amount sent against the SDG target of 3% (2026-08)
note: the figure is cited by AfricaNenda's deputy chief executive in an interview rather than drawn from a published series, and no date, corridor set or methodology is given for it, so it is a stated position and not a measurement the base can reproduce

subject: dpi.pay
name: Fintech volume carried by the continent's largest operator
milestone: Half-year results to 30 June 2026, published 2026-08-24
position_end: 13.0 billion transactions carrying US$330.5bn in the half, up 17.2% in volume and 33.8% in value in constant currency, on 70.8 million monthly active mobile-money users
note: the operator's own reporting, group-wide rather than Africa-only, and the group also reports markets outside the continent

subject: dpi.pay
name: Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS)
milestone: BEAC acceded on 2026-07-11
position_start: Operating from January 2022 across West and East African cores, with no Central African central bank participating
position_end: Extended into Central Africa by the BEAC's accession, wired into a national switch in Kenya for the first time, and carrying a wallet-based Nigeria-to-Ghana rail settled in naira
sources: 2026-07-09-beac-joins-papss-cross-border-payments-cemac-techafricanews|2026-03-02 Pesalink and PAPSS link networks for African payments|2026-02-04 PAPSS, Onafriq launch new trade rail for West Africa

subject: dpi.pay
name: PAPSSCARD
milestone: Launched with Afreximbank and Mercury Payment Services
position_end: A continental card scheme launched to route African card payments inside the continent rather than through global networks; no issuance, volume or country coverage held
sources: 2026-01-27 Nigeria's PAPSS cross-border payments falls 53% to N5.6bn

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payment Systems Directive for Africa (PSDA)
milestone: Decision 21 of the AACB Assembly of Governors, 2025-11-28
position_end: Directed to be led by central banks rather than an external entity, with the Assembly's own task force on payment system integration to lead harmonisation; no draft directive held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Stablecoin settlement rails serving African cross-border payments
milestone: Regulators from three states set out their approaches, 2026-08-18
position_end: Described by a pan-African payments operator's product chief as moving from speculative use into the plumbing of remittances and business settlement, on the evidence of Mastercard's agreement to acquire BVNK at up to US$1.8bn and Visa's stablecoin-card expansion through Stripe's Bridge into more than 100 countries, African markets among them; a first named African deployment is Flutterwave's tie-up with Caliza offering USD accounts with USDC and USDT conversion. At a UN Economic Commission for Africa webinar on 18 August 2026, market supervisors from Uganda's Capital Markets Authority, the Bank of Ghana and the Financial Services Commission of Mauritius set out three national approaches to virtual assets and stablecoins and agreed on consumer protection, financial stability, regulatory clarity and monetary sovereignty as shared objectives, arguing that compatible outcomes and supervisory cooperation matter more than identical legislation; the Commission put continental digital-asset users above 54 million, Nigeria alone at about 25.9 million, against a global tokenised money market that passed US$300bn in 2025
note: no African regulator has published a settled treatment of stablecoin settlement; what is held is three supervisors' accounts of their own approaches at a convened webinar, alongside an operator's account of its own market. Flutterwave and Caliza announced on 2026-08-13 dedicated USD accounts for African businesses on ACH, Fedwire, RTP and SWIFT with stablecoin conversion, aimed at cross-border transfers above US$1m - a commercial announcement carrying no volume, pricing or licensing detail

subject: dpi.pay
name: UnionPay online acceptance through Standard Bank
milestone: Extended to nine markets, announced 2026-08-19
position_start: A collaboration between the two parties dating from 2024, with no merchant count published
position_end: Online-payment acceptance for nearly 900 merchants across Botswana, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Namibia, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe, settling in local currency, US dollars or both, against a stated African footprint of about 7 million UnionPay cards issued
note: the merchant count, the card footprint and the market list are the two parties' own; no transaction volume, fee or settlement-currency split is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Unmet trade finance demand
position_end: US$74bn to US$100bn of unmet trade finance demand, with commercial banks intermediating about 23% of the continent's trade against 40% over 2011 to 2019, and intra-African trade at US$213.8bn in 2025 (2026-08)
note: a research firm's policy brief, which names digital payment rails, blockchain-enabled trade infrastructure and factoring as the routes to closing the gap. The financier's own May 2026 survey report puts the post-COVID gap at an average of US$74bn over 2021-24, against US$92.3bn averaged over 2011-19 and US$48.41bn in 2020

subject: dpi.mis
name: Africa CDC Central Data Repository
milestone: Launched 2026-01-28
position_end: A federated repository integrating national surveillance, laboratory and programme data in which member states retain ownership of their data
sources: 2026-01-28 Africa CDC Establishes Central Data Repository to Strengthen Public Health Surveillance
note: Financed by the Global Fund and prototyped by the Public Health Informatics Institute

subject: dpi.mis
name: African Initiative on Transforming Health Financing (ECA)
milestone: Launched Tangier, April 2026; runs 2026-2030
position_end: A five-year Economic Commission for Africa initiative running 2026 to 2030, launched in Tangier in April 2026, built on seven interlinked outcomes of which digital governance is one, alongside fiscal embedding, innovative financing instruments, primary health care modernisation, regional public goods, institutional capacity and narrative transformation. Its digital component is a shared data and intelligence platform for quantifying national financing gaps, real-time interoperable health and budget data, and what the Commission's chief of staff called a digital twin of the health budget underwriting multi-year compacts between finance and health ministries; the Commission puts fewer than a third of health systems in low-income settings as able to track spending digitally in real time, governments as financing under 41% of total health expenditure on average, and 30 to 40% of health spending as lost to inefficiency
note: the digital component is described in the Commission's own remarks to health ministers; no platform, procurement, budget line or delivery date is published for it

subject: dpi.mis
name: African Regional Integration Synthesized Index (ASRII) platform
milestone: ECOWAS Commission trained on the platform, Abuja, 4-7 August 2026
position_end: The African Union Commission's platform for submission, validation, automated computation and dissemination of regional integration scores across political, economic, infrastructure, and human and social pillars, developed with the regional economic communities, the Economic Commission for Africa and the African Development Bank to replace manual data collection. Deployment to the regional economic communities began with a four-day training of 20 core participants at the ECOWAS Commission in Abuja on 4-7 August 2026, at which its Secretary General said the Commission holds no centralised database of the status, amendments and implications of regional legal protocols
note: The platform is to be used by the regional economic communities to evaluate member states' policy implementation; no published score, methodology note or coverage list is held

subject: tech.ai
name: Africa AI Council
milestone: Established by the Smart Africa Board at Conakry, 2025-11-17
position_end: Established under a board of 42 heads of state with the AU Commissioner for Energy and Infrastructure and the ITU Secretary-General; no work programme or output held in the nine months since

subject: tech.ai
name: Africa AI Fund
milestone: Announced at Kigali, April 2025
position_start: Announced in April 2025 at US$60bn, alongside the Africa AI Declaration, with nothing capitalised
position_end: Still cited as one pillar of the continental AI architecture; no capitalisation, governance structure or disbursement held
sources: 2026-05-21 Pushing back from Big Tech Africa's hard road to AI sovereignty

subject: tech.ai
name: AU Continental AI Strategy
milestone: Adopted by the AU Executive Council, 45th Ordinary Session, Accra, 2024-07-19
position_start: Adopted 2024-07-19 as the continental reference for national AI policy, on an implementation timeframe running 2025 to 2030
position_end: Unchanged in text, and the reference the Commission carried into global forums; ministers meeting at the ECA called for its translation into national frameworks. The instrument's own timetable runs Phase I across 2025-2026, a midterm review in 2027 and Phase II from 2028
sources: 2024-07-19-au-continental-artificial-intelligence-strategy|2026-04-13 Stakeholders urge shift in digital public infrastructure trajectory|2026-07-09 African Union pushes for unified African voice at Global AI Governance Dialogue
note: Its annex records six member states with standalone national AI strategies at drafting in July 2024

subject: tech.ai
name: Common African Position on AI and its Impact on Peace, Security, Democracy and Development
milestone: Peace and Security Council requested finalisation, 1339th meeting, 2026-04-16
position_end: The Council requested the Commission to expedite the comprehensive study and the Common African Position and submit them for its consideration; a Policy Brief on AI for Peace, Security and Governance in Africa is reported in progress and no text is published

subject: tech.ai

position_end: A technology company offered African students one year of its paid artificial-intelligence assistant tier at no charge, pitched at study materials, assignments and planning

subject: tech.ai
name: Fund departmental paper on artificial intelligence in the region
milestone: Departmental paper published July 2026
position_end: A departmental paper on the potential of artificial intelligence across sub-Saharan Africa, held in full as published
note: an institution's analysis rather than a commitment or an instrument; it carries no financing, programme or country allocation

subject: tech.ai
name: Google Africa Applied AI Lab
milestone: Applications opened 2026-08-17 for a cohort running mid-September to early December 2026
position_end: A co-development programme based at the Accra AI Community Centre and run with the sponsor's AI futures fund, giving selected African startups from pre-seed to Series C+ pre-release access to its Gemini, Gemma and Veo models plus research mentorship and go-to-market support, with no equity taken and no cash award guaranteed; it closes with a demo day in Accra
note: cohort size and selection criteria are not stated

position_start: Provided for in the Strategy through an African AI readiness index, a public monitoring dashboard and regional AI observatories, with nothing published
position_end: Still nothing published; the Peace and Security Council requested the Commission and its AI Advisory Group to submit periodic reports on 2026-04-16, and the Strategy's own midterm review falls in 2027

subject: tech.ai
name: Pan-African AI governance research and advocacy project
milestone: Four-year programme running 2026-2030
position_end: A four-year research and advocacy project on pan-African AI governance, funded at EUR 1,873,314 and running 2026 to 2030, implemented by a consortium of a German university media research centre and three civil-society organisations; the position it argues from is common principles through continental institutions rather than 54 national AI regimes, covering data governance, AI ethics, procurement standards, regulatory sandboxes, cross-border research and capacity-building

subject: tech.ai
name: Public capital committed to the AU Continental AI Strategy
milestone: Gap set out at a policy academy, 2026-08-26
position_end: About US$150m of public capital committed by African governments against an implementation cost the Strategy itself prices at between US$250bn and US$500bn - a fraction of one per cent - and an ambition to add US$1.5 trillion to Africa's GDP by 2030; independent research over the Strategy's first eighteen months found the funding heavily concentrated in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa and Egypt, with little reaching the remaining member states
note: a policy analyst's figures reported by a single outlet; neither the commitment total nor the concentration finding is traced to a published AU accounting

subject: tech.industry

milestone: Announced to take effect 2026-10-01
position_start: Service messages on the business platform free of charge
position_end: Free service messages to end from 1 October 2026, with businesses charged for every delivered message at rates varying by country and by message type, a cost increase for African companies that rely heavily on the messenger for customer service
note: a platform pricing decision by a foreign operator, outside any African regulator's reach on the record held; the per-country rates are not published

milestone: Second cohort opened for applications, August 2026
position_end: A foundation-funded incubation programme opened applications for a second continental cohort of technology startups
note: a call for applications rather than an outcome; no cohort size, selection criterion, funding per company or first-cohort result is published

milestone: Procurement opened, bids due 2026-08-17
position_end: A EUR120,000 procurement opened by a European development agency for a multi-country mapping of African entrepreneurship- and innovation-support organisations under a Europe-Africa digital innovation programme
note: a procurement rather than an award; no supplier, country list or publication commitment for the mapping is stated

subject: include.divides

position_end: An industry-body accelerator backed by two private foundations opened its next call for digital-inclusion solutions for women and girls across India and sub-Saharan Africa, with a grant amount listed at INR 42,000,000

subject: geopol.usa
name: America First Global Health Strategy data-sharing agreements
milestone: Health cooperation memorandums signed with more than 30 countries since December 2025
movement: Advanced, refused by three states and challenged in the United States Senate
position_start: Did not exist; no bilateral United States health agreement of this kind on record before December 2025
position_end: Memorandums worth US$20bn signed with more than 30 countries since December 2025, on a model Data Sharing Agreement giving the United States at-will access to seven classes of national health system for 25 years with a 10-year post-termination tail; Ghana refused in April 2026, Zimbabwe withdrew in February 2026 and Zambia shelved in May 2026, and Kenya's framework is before the Court of Appeal with a final ruling due at the end of October 2026; the State Department's standard-form memorandum, held as a blank template dated 2026-03-11, commits a partner government to name and run its electronic medical record, laboratory, pharmacy, surveillance, commodity-inventory and national data warehouse systems, to load 90 per cent of clinical encounters into the electronic medical record within two years of rollout in a facility, to enter a data sharing agreement expected to run twenty-five years, and to provide specimens and genetic sequence data of pathogens with epidemic potential within five days of detection, with section 4.7 making failure on those commitments grounds for changing or discontinuing the assistance; the signed texts are withheld, the department having published a subset of the memorandums in March 2026 and then removed public access, and a freedom-of-information suit covering sixteen African countries (Public Citizen v. Department of State, No. 1:26-cv-01137, D.D.C.) was unresolved when filed on 2026-04-02; a rights organisation's clause-by-clause assessment of the seven signed memorandums it holds - Ethiopia, Kenya, Mozambique, Nigeria, Rwanda, Liberia and Uganda - reports that the model's terms were not applied uniformly: all seven require broad audit access, three (Liberia, Mozambique and Rwanda) commit to supplying any data requested for that audit with no privacy safeguard stated, two (Liberia and Nigeria) defer the data-sharing arrangement to an unpublished appendix, and the specimen and pathogen-sequencing clause appears in five of the seven, with Liberia and Kenya outside it Eight United States senators wrote to the Secretary of State in the week to 2026-08-19 challenging the demands for direct access to partner governments' own health-data systems as a condition of lifesaving aid, calling them unprecedented and at odds with United States policy on the data of American citizens, and requesting a briefing on the agreements' data requirements and a written answer by the end of August 2026.
note: The model Data Sharing Agreement's own text is not held; its terms are reported at second hand (2025-11-15). The standard-form memorandum is held as a blank template and is not any signatory's instrument. The seven signed texts remain withheld by the department: what is held of them is one organisation's assessment, itself drawn from leaks and from the subset briefly published in March 2026

subject: geopol.usa
name: US-AUC Strategic Investment Working Group
milestone: Launch announced in a joint statement, 2026-01-28
position_end: Agreed to channel US private investment into AU-backed infrastructure including digital transformation, on an investment-in-place-of-aid posture; no membership, meeting or work programme held
sources: 2026-01-28 Joint Statement of the United States and African Union on the Launch of a Strategic Investment Working Group

subject: geopol.china
name: ATU memorandum with the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology
milestone: Signed 2025; cited as the basis for the Hangzhou seminar, 2026-08-24
position_end: A memorandum signed in 2025 between the African Telecommunications Union and the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology on joint research, capacity development, technology transfer and next-generation networks, which the Union names as the foundation for its Secretary-General's participation in an Advanced Seminar on African Digital Development and Transformation that opened in Hangzhou on 24 August 2026, where he carried the priorities of its 52 member states
note: the memorandum is known only from the Union's own social-media account of it; no signing date, text, term, funding or work programme is held

subject: geopol.china
name: China-Africa Digital Cooperation Development Action Plan
milestone: Issued at the China-Africa Digital Cooperation Forum, Beijing, 2024-07-29
position_start: Issued 2024-07-29 by China and 26 African states across six cooperation actions, with a three-year target of ten joint digital transformation demonstration projects and 1,000 personnel trained
position_end: Unchanged; no progress report, no accession beyond the original 26 states and no delivery against the three-year targets is held
note: Signed by states individually rather than by the African Union; no sum appears anywhere in the plan

subject: geopol.china
name: Chinese artificial-intelligence cooperation centres with the African Union
milestone: First high-level training programme opened at Hangzhou, August 2026
position_end: The first high-level training programme on digital development and transformation opened at Hangzhou in August 2026, giving the announced cooperation its first delivered activity; the announcement had promised application cooperation centres with the African Union and 5,000 training places for developing countries over five years, and no site, budget or term is published for the centres themselves
note: a training programme is not a centre; the participant count, the African states represented and the curriculum are unpublished
